correctness.rationale: For any two characters, factoring the \(2\times2\) restriction determinant leaves the nonzero factor \(\psi(d_j)-1\), so one quotient character outside all annihilators is necessary and sufficient. Each annihilator has size \(|G|/o(d_j)\le|G|/p\) and all contain the trivial character; the overlap-aware union estimate is strictly below \(|G|\) for \(m\le p\). In \(\mathbb Z_p^2\), the annihilators of representatives of the \(p+1\) directions are exactly all dual lines and cover the dual. The actual verifier exhaustively checks the determinant equivalence and small-group threshold examples.

final_claim: For two-point subsets \(E_j=\{x_j,y_j\}\) of a finite abelian group, a simultaneous exponential Riesz basis exists exactly when the annihilators \((y_j-x_j)^\perp\) do not cover the dual group. If \(p\) is the least prime divisor of \(|G|\), every family of at most \(p\) such sets has a common basis, and \(p+1\) can fail in \(\mathbb Z_p^2\); in particular every pair has a common basis.
limitations: Only two-point subsets; no claim for cardinality three or larger.
No quantitative conditioning bound is claimed.
